#### pub fn [eventual_consistency](https://docs.rs#method.eventual_consistency)(self) -> Self

Rather than read data from the primary data source, which is slower but strongly consistent (`strong`, the default), instead read a local copy if available, which offers higher speed and may be a few seconds out of date (`eventual`).

Set the maximum number of items included the response. The default limit is 100 items.

Set the prefix match for items to include in the resultset.

# LookupBuilder in fastly - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fastly/0.13.0/fastly/struct.LookupBuilder.html

`pub struct LookupBuilder<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A builder for KVStore lookups, supporting advanced features like asynchronous execution.

```
store.build_lookup()
   .execute("key1")?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#synchronous-and-asynchronous-support)Synchronous and Asynchronous support

LookupBuilder exposes the ability to issue an asynchronous lookup. Using
[ execute_async](https://docs.rs/struct.LookupBuilder.html#method.execute_async) will send the request, and unblock. There is currently no polling mechanism.
To retrieve the result, use the blocking function

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.KVStore.html#method.pending_lookup_wait)

`pending_lookup_wait`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
// synchronous non-builder lookup
let result: Result<LookupResponse, KVStoreError> = store.lookup("key");
// synchronous builder lookup
let result: Result<LookupResponse, KVStoreError> = store.build_lookup().execute("key");
// asynchronous builder lookup
let lookup_handle: Result<PendingLookupHandle, KVStoreError> = store.build_lookup().execute_async("key");
let result: Result<LookupResponse, KVStoreError> = store.pending_lookup_wait(lookup_handle?);
```

# Request in fastly - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fastly/0.13.0/fastly/struct.Request.html

`pub struct Request { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An HTTP request, including body, headers, method, and URL.

[§](https://docs.rs#getting-the-client-request)Getting the client request

Call [ Request::from_client()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.from_client) to get the client request being handled by this execution of the
Compute program.

[§](https://docs.rs#creation-and-conversion)Creation and conversion

New requests can be created programmatically with [ Request::new()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.new). In addition, there are
convenience constructors like

[which automatically select the appropriate method.](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.get)

`Request::get()`For interoperability with other Rust libraries, [ Request](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html) can be converted to and from the

[crate’s](https://docs.rs/http/1.3.1/wasm32-wasip1/http/index.html)

`http`[type using the](https://docs.rs/http/1.3.1/wasm32-wasip1/http/request/struct.Request.html)

`http::Request`[and](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.from)

`From`[traits.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html#tymethod.into)

`Into`[§](https://docs.rs#sending-backend-requests)Sending backend requests

Requests can be sent to a backend in blocking or asynchronous fashion using
[ send()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send),

[, or](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send_async)

`send_async()`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send_async_streaming)

`send_async_streaming()`[§](https://docs.rs#builder-style-methods)Builder-style methods

[ Request](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html) can be used as a

[builder](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.0.0/style/ownership/builders.html), allowing requests to be constructed and used through method chaining. Methods with the

`with_` name prefix, such as
[, return](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.with_header)

`with_header()``Self` to allow chaining. The builder style is
typically most useful when constructing and using a request in a single expression. For example:```
Request::get("https://example.com")
    .with_header("my-header", "hello!")
    .with_header("my-other-header", "Здравствуйте!")
    .send("example_backend")?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#setter-methods)Setter methods

Setter methods, such as [ set_header()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_header), are prefixed by

`set_`, and can
be used interchangeably with the builder-style methods, allowing you to mix and match styles
based on what is most convenient for your program. Setter methods tend to work better than
builder-style methods when constructing a request involves conditional branches or loops. For
example:```
let mut req = Request::get("https://example.com").with_header("my-header", "hello!");
if needs_translation {
    req.set_header("my-other-header", "Здравствуйте!");
}
req.send("example_backend")?;
```

[the low-level handle API](https://docs.rs/handle/index.html).

[to populate the request argument. Use an undecorated](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.from_client)

`Request::from_client()``main()` function instead, along with [or](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.send_to_client)

`ToUrl`[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#390-396)#### pub fn [clone_without_body](https://docs.rs#method.clone_without_body)(&self) -> [Request](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#390-396)

#### pub fn [clone_without_body](https://docs.rs#method.clone_without_body)(&self) -> [Request](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html)

Make a new request with the same method, url, headers, and version of this request, but no body.

If you also need to clone the request body, use
`clone_with_body()`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
let original = Request::post("https://example.com")
    .with_header("hello", "world!")
    .with_body("hello");
let new = original.clone_without_body();
assert_eq!(original.get_method(), new.get_method());
assert_eq!(original.get_url(), new.get_url());
assert_eq!(original.get_header("hello"), new.get_header("hello"));
assert_eq!(original.get_version(), new.get_version());
assert!(original.has_body());
assert!(!new.has_body());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#420-452)#### pub fn [clone_with_body](https://docs.rs#method.clone_with_body)(&mut self) -> [Request](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#420-452)

#### pub fn [clone_with_body](https://docs.rs#method.clone_with_body)(&mut self) -> [Request](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html)

Clone this request by reading in its body, and then writing the same body to the original and the cloned request.

This method requires mutable access to this request because reading from and writing to the body can involve an HTTP connection.

This operation is potentially expensive if the body is large. Take care when using this
method on bodies with unknown sizes. Consider using methods like [ BufRead::lines()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.BufRead.html#method.lines) or

[to incrementally process a body while limiting the maximum size.](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html#method.read_chunks)

`Body::read_chunks()`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
let mut original = Request::post("https://example.com")
    .with_header("hello", "world!")
    .with_body("hello");
let mut new = original.clone_with_body();
assert_eq!(original.get_method(), new.get_method());
assert_eq!(original.get_url(), new.get_url());
assert_eq!(original.get_header("hello"), new.get_header("hello"));
assert_eq!(original.get_version(), new.get_version());
assert_eq!(original.take_body_bytes(), new.take_body_bytes());
```

#### pub fn [set_before_send](https://docs.rs#method.set_before_send)(
    &mut self,
    f: impl [Fn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.Fn.html)(&mut [Request](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [SendErrorCause](https://docs.rs/http/request/enum.SendErrorCause.html)> + [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + [Sync](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html) + 'static,
)

Sets a callback to be invoked if a request misses the cache, allowing the request to be modified beforehand.

This callback is useful when, for example, a backend requires an additional header to be inserted, but that header is expensive to produce. The callback will only be invoked if the original request cannot be responded to from the cache, so the header is only computed when it is truly needed.

Note that the callback is only invoked if the request is a candidate for caching; it is not
invoked if the request is explicitly to the backend with [ Request::set_pass()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_pass).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#547-553)#### pub fn [with_after_send](https://docs.rs#method.with_after_send)(

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#564-571)

#### pub fn [set_after_send](https://docs.rs#method.set_after_send)(
    &mut self,
    f: impl [Fn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.Fn.html)(&mut [CandidateResponse](https://docs.rs/http/struct.CandidateResponse.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [SendErrorCause](https://docs.rs/http/request/enum.SendErrorCause.html)> + [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + [Sync](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html) + 'static,
)

Sets a callback to be invoked after a response is returned from a backend, but before it is stored into the cache.

This callback allows for cache properties like TTL to be customized beyond what the backend resopnse headers specify. It also allows for the response itself to be modified prior to storing into the cache.

Note that the callback is only invoked if the request is a candidate for caching; it is not
invoked if the request is explicitly to the backend with [ Request::set_pass()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_pass).

Retrieve a reponse for the request, either from cache or by sending it to the given backend server. Returns once the response headers have been received, or an error occurs.

[§](https://docs.rs#argument-type-conversion-10)Argument type conversion

The backend argument can be any type that implements [ ToBackend](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToBackend.html); see that trait for details on
which types can be used and when panics may arise during conversion.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

Sending the client request to a backend without modification:

```
let backend_resp = Request::from_client().send("example_backend").expect("request succeeds");
assert!(backend_resp.get_status().is_success());
```
Sending a synthetic request:

```
let backend_resp = Request::get("https://example.com")
    .send("example_backend")
    .expect("request succeeds");
assert!(backend_resp.get_status().is_success());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#772-802)#### pub fn [send_async](https://docs.rs#method.send_async)(
    self,
    backend: impl [ToBackend](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToBackend.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[PendingRequest](https://docs.rs/http/request/struct.PendingRequest.html), [SendError](https://docs.rs/http/request/struct.SendError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#772-802)

#### pub fn [send_async](https://docs.rs#method.send_async)(
    self,
    backend: impl [ToBackend](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToBackend.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[PendingRequest](https://docs.rs/http/request/struct.PendingRequest.html), [SendError](https://docs.rs/http/request/struct.SendError.html)>

Begin sending the request to the given backend server, and return a [ PendingRequest](https://docs.rs/http/request/struct.PendingRequest.html) that
can yield the backend response or an error.

This method returns as soon as the request begins sending to the backend, and transmission of the request body and headers will continue in the background.

This method allows for sending more than one request at once and receiving their responses
in arbitrary orders. See [ PendingRequest](https://docs.rs/http/request/struct.PendingRequest.html) for more details on how to wait on, poll, or
select between pending requests.

This method is also useful for sending requests where the response is unimportant, but the request may take longer than the Compute program is able to run, as the request will continue sending even after the program that initiated it exits.

[§](https://docs.rs#argument-type-conversion-11)Argument type conversion

The backend argument can be any type that implements [ ToBackend](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToBackend.html); see that trait for details on
which types can be used and when panics may arise during conversion.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

Sending a request to two backends and returning whichever response finishes first:

```
let backend_resp_1 = Request::get("https://example.com/")
    .send_async("example_backend_1")
    .expect("request 1 begins sending");
let backend_resp_2 = Request::get("https://example.com/")
    .send_async("example_backend_2")
    .expect("request 2 begins sending");
let (resp, _) = fastly::http::request::select(vec![backend_resp_1, backend_resp_2]);
resp.expect("request succeeds").send_to_client();
```
Sending a long-running request and ignoring its result so that the program can exit before it completes:

```
let _ = Request::post("https://example.com")
    .with_body(some_large_file)
    .send_async("example_backend");
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#853-885)#### pub fn [send_async_streaming](https://docs.rs#method.send_async_streaming)(
    self,
    backend: impl [ToBackend](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToBackend.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<([StreamingBody](https://docs.rs/http/body/struct.StreamingBody.html), [PendingRequest](https://docs.rs/http/request/struct.PendingRequest.html)), [SendError](https://docs.rs/http/request/struct.SendError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#853-885)

#### pub fn [send_async_streaming](https://docs.rs#method.send_async_streaming)(
    self,
    backend: impl [ToBackend](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToBackend.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<([StreamingBody](https://docs.rs/http/body/struct.StreamingBody.html), [PendingRequest](https://docs.rs/http/request/struct.PendingRequest.html)), [SendError](https://docs.rs/http/request/struct.SendError.html)>

Begin sending the request to the given backend server, and return a [ PendingRequest](https://docs.rs/http/request/struct.PendingRequest.html) that
can yield the backend response or an error along with a

[that can accept further data to send.](https://docs.rs/http/body/struct.StreamingBody.html)

`StreamingBody`The backend connection is only closed once [ StreamingBody::finish()](https://docs.rs/http/body/struct.StreamingBody.html#method.finish) is called. The

[will not yield a](https://docs.rs/http/request/struct.PendingRequest.html)

`PendingRequest`[until the](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html)

`Response`[is finished.](https://docs.rs/http/body/struct.StreamingBody.html)

`StreamingBody`This method is most useful for programs that do some sort of processing or inspection of a potentially-large client request body. Streaming allows the program to operate on small parts of the body rather than having to read it all into memory at once.

This method returns as soon as the request begins sending to the backend, and transmission of the request body and headers will continue in the background.

Note that the implementation of `send_async_streaming` does not currently support also using
[Request::set_before_send](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_before_send) or [Request::set_after_send](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_after_send). Attempts to call this method after
also setting the callbacks will result in an [SendErrorCause::HttpCacheApiUnsupported](https://docs.rs/http/request/enum.SendErrorCause.html#variant.HttpCacheApiUnsupported)
error.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

Count the number of lines in a UTF-8 client request body while sending it to the backend:

```
use std::io::{BufRead, Write};
let mut req = Request::from_client();
// Take the body so we can iterate through its lines later
let req_body = req.take_body();
// Start sending the client request to the client with a now-empty body
let (mut backend_body, pending_req) = req
    .send_async_streaming("example_backend")
    .expect("request begins sending");
let mut num_lines = 0;
for line in req_body.lines() {
    let line = line?;
    num_lines += 1;
    // Write the line to the streaming backend body
    backend_body.write_all(line.as_bytes())?;
}
// Finish the streaming body to allow the backend connection to close
backend_body.finish()?;
println!("client request body contained {} lines", num_lines);
```

#### pub fn [get_body_prefix_str_mut](https://docs.rs#method.get_body_prefix_str_mut)(&mut self, length: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [PrefixString](https://docs.rs/http/body/struct.PrefixString.html)<'_>

Get a prefix of this request’s body as a string containing up to the given number of bytes.

See [ Body::get_prefix_str_mut()](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html#method.get_prefix_str_mut) for details.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-1)Panics

If the prefix contains invalid UTF-8 bytes, this function will panic. The exception to this is if the bytes are invalid because a multi-byte codepoint is cut off by the requested prefix length. In this case, the invalid bytes are left off the end of the prefix.

To explicitly handle the possibility of invalid UTF-8 bytes, use
[ try_get_body_prefix_str_mut()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.try_get_body_prefix_str_mut), which returns an
error on failure rather than panicking.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1022-1028)#### pub fn [append_body](https://docs.rs#method.append_body)(&mut self, other: [Body](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1022-1028)

#### pub fn [append_body](https://docs.rs#method.append_body)(&mut self, other: [Body](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html))

Append another [ Body](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html) to the body of this request without reading or writing any body
contents.

If this request does not have a body, the appended body is set as the request’s body.

This operation is performed in amortized constant time, and so should always be preferred to reading an entire body and then writing the same contents to another body.

This method should be used when combining bodies that have not necessarily been read yet,
such as the body of the client. To append contents that are already in memory as strings or
bytes, you should instead use [ get_body_mut()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.get_body_mut) to write the
contents to the end of the body.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-7)Examples

```
let mut req = Request::post("https://example.com").with_body("hello! client says: ");
req.append_body(Request::from_client().into_body());
req.send("example_backend")?;
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1041-1043)#### pub fn [into_body_bytes](https://docs.rs#method.into_body_bytes)(self) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1041-1043)

#### pub fn [into_body_bytes](https://docs.rs#method.into_body_bytes)(self) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Consume the request and return its body as a byte vector.

[§](https://docs.rs#memory-usage)Memory usage

This method will cause the entire body to be buffering in WebAssembly memory. You should take care
not to exceed the WebAssembly memory limits, and consider using methods like
[ read_body_lines()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.read_body_lines) or

[to control how much of the body you process at once.](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.read_body_chunks)

`read_body_chunks()`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
let req = Request::post("https://example.com").with_body_text_plain("hello, world!");
let bytes = req.into_body_bytes();
assert_eq!(&bytes, b"hello, world!");
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1165-1171)#### pub fn [take_body_str](https://docs.rs#method.take_body_str)(&mut self) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1165-1171)

#### pub fn [take_body_str](https://docs.rs#method.take_body_str)(&mut self) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

Take and return the body from this request as a string.

After calling this method, this request will no longer have a body.

[§](https://docs.rs#memory-usage-3)Memory usage

This method will cause the entire body to be buffering in WebAssembly memory. You should take care
not to exceed the WebAssembly memory limits, and consider using methods like
[ read_body_lines()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.read_body_lines) or

[to control how much of the body you process at once.](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.read_body_chunks)

`read_body_chunks()`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-3)Panics

If the body does not contain a valid UTF-8 string, this function will panic. To handle the
possibility of invalid UTF-8 data, use [ take_body_str_lossy()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.take_body_str_lossy) for
lossy conversion, or use

[and then convert the bytes with a function like](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.take_body_bytes)

`take_body_bytes()`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.from_utf8)

`String::from_utf8`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-13)Examples

```
let mut req = Request::post("https://example.com").with_body("hello, world!");
let string = req.take_body_str();
assert!(req.try_take_body().is_none());
assert_eq!(&string, "hello, world!");
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1191-1197)#### pub fn [take_body_str_lossy](https://docs.rs#method.take_body_str_lossy)(&mut self) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1191-1197)

Take and return the body from this request as a string, including invalid characters.

Only the valid UTF-8 characters present are returned.
Invalid UTF-8 characters are replaced with [ U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/char/constant.REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER.html).

After calling this method, this request will no longer have a body.

[§](https://docs.rs#memory-usage-4)Memory usage

This method will cause the entire body to be buffering in WebAssembly memory. You should take care
not to exceed the WebAssembly memory limits, and consider using methods like
[ read_body_lines()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.read_body_lines) or

[to control how much of the body you process at once.](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.read_body_chunks)

`read_body_chunks()`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-14)Examples

```
let mut req = Request::post("https://example.com");
req.set_body_octet_stream(b"\xF0\x90\x80 hello, world!");
let string = req.take_body_str_lossy();

assert_eq!(&string, "� hello, world!");
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1216-1218)#### pub fn [read_body_lines](https://docs.rs#method.read_body_lines)(&mut self) -> [Lines](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/struct.Lines.html)<&mut [Body](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1216-1218)

#### pub fn [read_body_lines](https://docs.rs#method.read_body_lines)(&mut self) -> [Lines](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/struct.Lines.html)<&mut [Body](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html)>

Return a [ Lines](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/struct.Lines.html) iterator that reads the request body a line at a time.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-15)Examples

```
use std::io::Write;
fn remove_es(req: &mut Request) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let mut no_es = Body::new();
    for line in req.read_body_lines() {
        writeln!(no_es, "{}", line.unwrap().replace("e", ""))?;
    }
    req.set_body(no_es);
    Ok(())
}
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1290-1295)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1290-1295)

Return an iterator that reads the request body in chunks of at most the given number of bytes.

If `chunk_size` does not evenly divide the length of the body, then the last chunk will not
have length `chunk_size`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-18)Examples

```
use std::io::Write;
fn remove_0s(req: &mut Request) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let mut no_0s = Body::new();
    for chunk in req.read_body_chunks(4096) {
        let mut chunk = chunk?;
        chunk.retain(|b| *b != 0);
        no_0s.write_all(&chunk)?;
    }
    req.set_body(no_0s);
    Ok(())
}
```
Convert the given value to JSON and set that JSON as the request’s body.

The given value must implement [ serde::Serialize](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/wasm32-wasip1/serde_core/ser/trait.Serialize.html). You can either implement that trait for
your own custom type, or use

[to create untyped JSON values. See](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.145/wasm32-wasip1/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html)

`serde_json::Value`[for details.](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.145/wasm32-wasip1/serde_json/index.html)

`serde_json`Any previous body that may have been set on the response is discarded. To add to an existing body,
use [ get_body_mut()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.get_body_mut) and write to the returned

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html)

`Body`[§](https://docs.rs#content-type-3)Content type

This method sets the content type to `application/json`.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

This method returns [ serde_json::Error](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.145/wasm32-wasip1/serde_json/error/struct.Error.html) if serialization fails.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-19)Examples

Using a type that derives [ serde::Serialize](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/wasm32-wasip1/serde_core/ser/trait.Serialize.html):

```
#[derive(serde::Serialize)]
struct MyData {
    name: String,
    count: u64,
}
let my_data = MyData { name: "Computers".to_string(), count: 1024 };
let mut req = Request::post("https://example.com");
req.set_body_json(&my_data).unwrap();
assert_eq!(req.get_content_type(), Some(fastly::mime::APPLICATION_JSON));
assert_eq!(&req.into_body_str(), r#"{"name":"Computers","count":1024}"#);
```
Using untyped JSON and the [ serde_json::json](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.145/wasm32-wasip1/serde_json/macro.json.html) macro:

```
let my_data = serde_json::json!({
    "name": "Computers",
    "count": 1024,
});
let mut req = Request::post("https://example.com");
req.set_body_json(&my_data).unwrap();
assert_eq!(req.get_content_type(), Some(fastly::mime::APPLICATION_JSON));
assert_eq!(&req.into_body_str(), r#"{"count":1024,"name":"Computers"}"#);
```

#### pub fn [take_body_json](https://docs.rs#method.take_body_json)<T: [DeserializeOwned](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/wasm32-wasip1/serde_core/de/trait.DeserializeOwned.html)>(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, [Error](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.145/wasm32-wasip1/serde_json/error/struct.Error.html)>

Take the request body and attempt to parse it as a JSON value.

The return type must implement [ serde::Deserialize](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/wasm32-wasip1/serde_core/de/trait.Deserialize.html) without any non-static lifetimes. You
can either implement that trait for your own custom type, or use

[to deserialize untyped JSON values. See](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.145/wasm32-wasip1/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html)

`serde_json::Value`[for details.](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.145/wasm32-wasip1/serde_json/index.html)

`serde_json`After calling this method, this request will no longer have a body.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-1)Errors

This method returns [ serde_json::Error](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.145/wasm32-wasip1/serde_json/error/struct.Error.html) if deserialization fails.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-20)Examples

Using a type that derives [ serde::de::DeserializeOwned](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/wasm32-wasip1/serde_core/de/trait.DeserializeOwned.html):

```
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct MyData {
    name: String,
    count: u64,
}
let mut req = Request::post("https://example.com")
    .with_body(r#"{"name":"Computers","count":1024}"#);
let my_data = req.take_body_json::<MyData>().unwrap();
assert_eq!(&my_data.name, "Computers");
assert_eq!(my_data.count, 1024);
```
Using untyped JSON with [ serde_json::Value](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.145/wasm32-wasip1/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html):

```
let my_data = serde_json::json!({
    "name": "Computers",
    "count": 1024,
});
let mut req = Request::post("https://example.com")
    .with_body(r#"{"name":"Computers","count":1024}"#);
let my_data = req.take_body_json::<serde_json::Value>().unwrap();
assert_eq!(my_data["name"].as_str(), Some("Computers"));
assert_eq!(my_data["count"].as_u64(), Some(1024));
```

details.

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1598-1608)#### pub fn [get_header_str](https://docs.rs#method.get_header_str)(&self, name: impl [ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>

If there are multiple values for the header, only one is returned, which may be any of the
values. See [ get_header_all_str()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.get_header_all_str) if you need to get all of

details on which types can be used and when panics may arise during conversion.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-5)Panics

This method panics if the value of the header is not a valid UTF-8 string. To handle the possibility
of invalid UTF-8 data, use [ get_header_str_lossy()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.get_header_str_lossy) for lossy
conversion, or use

[and then convert the bytes with](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.get_header)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1631-1634)#### pub fn [get_header_str_lossy](https://docs.rs#method.get_header_str_lossy)(
    &self,
    name: impl [ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Cow](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/borrow/enum.Cow.html)<'_, [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1631-1634)

#### pub fn [get_header_str_lossy](https://docs.rs#method.get_header_str_lossy)(
    &self,
    name: impl [ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Cow](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/borrow/enum.Cow.html)<'_, [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>>

Get the value of a header as a string, including invalid characters, or `None` if the header
is not present.

Only the valid UTF-8 characters present are returned.
Invalid UTF-8 characters are replaced with [ U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/char/constant.REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER.html).

If there are multiple values for the header, only one is returned, which may be any of the
values. See [ get_header_all_str_lossy()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.get_header_all_str_lossy) if you need
to get all of the values.

[§](https://docs.rs#argument-type-conversion-15)Argument type conversion

The header name argument can be any type that implements [ ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html); see that trait for
details on which types can be used and when panics may arise during conversion.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-27)Examples

```
let header_value = HeaderValue::from_bytes(b"\xF0\x90\x80 world!").unwrap();
let req = Request::get("https://example.com").with_header("hello", header_value);
assert_eq!(req.get_header_str_lossy("hello"), Some(Cow::from("� world")));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1663-1665)#### pub fn [get_header](https://docs.rs#method.get_header)(&self, name: impl [ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[HeaderValue](https://docs.rs/http/struct.HeaderValue.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1663-1665)

#### pub fn [get_header](https://docs.rs#method.get_header)(&self, name: impl [ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[HeaderValue](https://docs.rs/http/struct.HeaderValue.html)>

Get the value of a header, or `None` if the header is not present.

If there are multiple values for the header, only one is returned, which may be any of the
values. See [ get_header_all()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.get_header_all) if you need to get all of the
values.

[§](https://docs.rs#argument-type-conversion-16)Argument type conversion

The header name argument can be any type that implements [ ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html); see that trait for
details on which types can be used and when panics may arise during conversion.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-28)Examples

Handling UTF-8 values explicitly:

```
let req = Request::get("https://example.com").with_header("hello", "world!");
assert_eq!(req.get_header("hello"), Some(&HeaderValue::from_static("world")));
```
Safely handling invalid UTF-8 values:

```
let invalid_utf8 = &"🐈".as_bytes()[0..3];
let req = Request::get("https://example.com").with_header("hello", invalid_utf8);
assert_eq!(req.get_header("hello").unwrap().as_bytes(), invalid_utf8);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1687-1695)#### pub fn [get_header_all_str](https://docs.rs#method.get_header_all_str)(&self, name: impl [ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html)) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1687-1695)

#### pub fn [get_header_all_str](https://docs.rs#method.get_header_all_str)(&self, name: impl [ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html)) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>

Get all values of a header as strings, or an empty vector if the header is not present.

[§](https://docs.rs#argument-type-conversion-17)Argument type conversion

The header name argument can be any type that implements [ ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html); see that trait for
details on which types can be used and when panics may arise during conversion.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-6)Panics

This method panics if any of the header values are not valid UTF-8 strings. To handle the
possibility of non-UTF-8 data, use
[ get_header_all_str_lossy()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.get_header_all_str_lossy) for lossy conversion, or use

[and then convert the bytes with](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.get_header_all)

`get_header_all()`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/str/converts/fn.from_utf8.html)

`std::str::from_utf8()`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-29)Examples

```
let req = Request::get("https://example.com")
    .with_header("hello", "world!")
    .with_header("hello", "universe!");
let values = req.get_header_all_str("hello");
assert_eq!(values.len(), 2);
assert!(values.contains(&"world!"));
assert!(values.contains(&"universe!"));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1719-1723)#### pub fn [get_header_all_str_lossy](https://docs.rs#method.get_header_all_str_lossy)(
    &self,
    name: impl [ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html),
) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Cow](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/borrow/enum.Cow.html)<'_, [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1719-1723)

#### pub fn [get_header_all_str_lossy](https://docs.rs#method.get_header_all_str_lossy)(
    &self,
    name: impl [ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html),
) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Cow](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/borrow/enum.Cow.html)<'_, [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>>

Get all values of a header as strings, including invalid characters, or an empty vector if the header is not present.

Only the valid UTF-8 characters present are returned.
Invalid UTF-8 characters are replaced with [ U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/char/constant.REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#argument-type-conversion-18)Argument type conversion

The header name argument can be any type that implements [ ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html); see that trait for
details on which types can be used and when panics may arise during conversion.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-30)Examples

```
let world_value = HeaderValue::from_bytes(b"\xF0\x90\x80 world!").unwrap();
let universe_value = HeaderValue::from_bytes(b"\xF0\x90\x80 universe!").unwrap();
let req = Request::get("https://example.com")
    .with_header("hello", world_value)
    .with_header("hello", universe_value);
let values = req.get_header_all_str_lossy("hello");
assert_eq!(values.len(), 2);
assert!(values.contains(&Cow::from("� world!")));
assert!(values.contains(&Cow::from("� universe!")));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1764-1766)#### pub fn [get_header_all](https://docs.rs#method.get_header_all)(
    &self,
    name: impl [ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html),
) -> impl [Iterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html)<Item = &[HeaderValue](https://docs.rs/http/struct.HeaderValue.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1764-1766)

#### pub fn [get_header_all](https://docs.rs#method.get_header_all)(
    &self,
    name: impl [ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html),
) -> impl [Iterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html)<Item = &[HeaderValue](https://docs.rs/http/struct.HeaderValue.html)>

Get an iterator of all the values of a header.

[§](https://docs.rs#argument-type-conversion-19)Argument type conversion

The header name argument can be any type that implements [ ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html); see that trait for
details on which types can be used and when panics may arise during conversion.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-31)Examples

You can turn the iterator into collection, like [ Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html):

```
let invalid_utf8 = &"🐈".as_bytes()[0..3];
let req = Request::get("https://example.com")
    .with_header("hello", "world!")
    .with_header("hello", invalid_utf8);
let values: Vec<&HeaderValue> = req.get_header_all("hello").collect();
assert_eq!(values.len(), 2);
assert!(values.contains(&&HeaderValue::from_static("world!")));
assert!(values.contains(&&HeaderValue::from_bytes(invalid_utf8).unwrap()));
```
You can use the iterator in a loop:

```
let invalid_utf8 = &"🐈".as_bytes()[0..3];
let req = Request::get("https://example.com")
    .with_header("hello", "world!")
    .with_header("hello", invalid_utf8);
for value in req.get_header_all("hello") {
    if let Ok(s) = std::str::from_utf8(value.as_bytes()) {
        println!("hello, {}", s);
    } else {
        println!("hello, invalid UTF-8!");
    }
}
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1799-1801)#### pub fn [get_headers](https://docs.rs#method.get_headers)(&self) -> impl [Iterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html)<Item = (&[HeaderName](https://docs.rs/http/struct.HeaderName.html), &[HeaderValue](https://docs.rs/http/struct.HeaderValue.html))>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1799-1801)

#### pub fn [get_headers](https://docs.rs#method.get_headers)(&self) -> impl [Iterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html)<Item = (&[HeaderName](https://docs.rs/http/struct.HeaderName.html), &[HeaderValue](https://docs.rs/http/struct.HeaderValue.html))>

Get an iterator of all the request’s header names and values.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-32)Examples

You can turn the iterator into a collection, like [ Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html):

```
let req = Request::get("https://example.com")
    .with_header("hello", "world!")
    .with_header("hello", "universe!");
let headers: Vec<(&HeaderName, &HeaderValue)> = req.get_headers().collect();
assert_eq!(headers.len(), 2);
assert!(headers.contains(&(&HeaderName::from_static("hello"), &HeaderValue::from_static("world!"))));
assert!(headers.contains(&(&HeaderName::from_static("hello"), &HeaderValue::from_static("universe!"))));
```
You can use the iterator in a loop:

```
let req = Request::get("https://example.com")
    .with_header("hello", "world!")
    .with_header("hello", "universe!");
for (n, v) in req.get_headers() {
    println!("Header -  {}: {:?}", n, v);
}
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1878-1881)#### pub fn [set_header](https://docs.rs#method.set_header)(&mut self, name: impl [ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html), value: impl [ToHeaderValue](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderValue.html))

Set a request header to the given value, discarding any previous values for the given header name.

The header name and value arguments can be any types that implement [ ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html) and

[, respectively. See those traits for details on which types can be used and when panics may arise during conversion.](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderValue.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1906-1909)#### pub fn [append_header](https://docs.rs#method.append_header)(

#### pub fn [append_header](https://docs.rs#method.append_header)(

Add a request header with given value.

Unlike [ set_header()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_header), this does not discard existing values for the
same header name.

[§](https://docs.rs#argument-type-conversion-21)Argument type conversion

The header name and value arguments can be any types that implement [ ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html) and

[, respectively. See those traits for details on which types can be used and when panics may arise during conversion.](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderValue.html)

`ToHeaderValue`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-36)Examples

```
let mut req = Request::get("https://example.com");

assert_eq!(req.get_header_str("hello"), Some("world!"));
req.append_header("hello", "universe!");
let values = req.get_header_all_str("hello");
assert_eq!(values.len(), 2);
assert!(values.contains(&"world!"));
assert!(values.contains(&"universe!"));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1928-1931)#### pub fn [remove_header](https://docs.rs#method.remove_header)(&mut self, name: impl [ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[HeaderValue](https://docs.rs/http/struct.HeaderValue.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1928-1931)

#### pub fn [remove_header](https://docs.rs#method.remove_header)(&mut self, name: impl [ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[HeaderValue](https://docs.rs/http/struct.HeaderValue.html)>

Remove all request headers of the given name, and return one of the removed header values if any were present.

If the header has multiple values, one is returned arbitrarily. To get all of the removed header
values, use [ get_header_all()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.get_header_all) before removing.

[§](https://docs.rs#argument-type-conversion-22)Argument type conversion

The header name argument can be any type that implements [ ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html); see that trait for
details on which types can be used and when panics may arise during conversion.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-37)Examples

```
let mut req = Request::get("https://example.com").with_header("hello", "world!");
assert_eq!(req.get_header_str("hello"), Some("world!"));
assert_eq!(req.remove_header("hello"), Some(HeaderValue::from_static("world!")));
assert!(req.remove_header("not-present").is_none());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#1953-1960)#### pub fn [remove_header_str](https://docs.rs#method.remove_header_str)(&mut self, name: impl [ToHeaderName](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.ToHeaderName.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>

If the header has multiple values, one is returned arbitrarily. To get all of the removed header
values, use [ get_header_all()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.get_header_all) before removing.

This method panics if the value of the header is not a valid UTF-8 string. To handle the possibility
of invalid UTF-8 data, use [ remove_header_str_lossy()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.remove_header_str_lossy) for lossy

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-41)Examples

```
use fastly::http::Method;
fn log_method(req: &Request) {
    match req.get_method() {
        &Method::GET | &Method::HEAD => println!("method was a GET or HEAD"),
        &Method::POST => println!("method was a POST"),
        _ => println!("method was something else"),
    }
}

#### pub fn [get_url_mut](https://docs.rs#method.get_url_mut)(&mut self) -> impl [DerefMut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/deref/trait.DerefMut.html)<Target = [Url](https://docs.rs/http/struct.Url.html)> + '_

Get a mutable reference to the request URL.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-45)Examples

```
let mut req = Request::get("https://example.com/");
let mut url = req.get_url_mut();
url.set_path("/hello");
url.set_fragment(Some("world"));
drop(url);
assert_eq!(req.get_url_str(), "https://example.com/hello#world");
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#2141-2143)#### pub fn [get_query_str](https://docs.rs#method.get_query_str)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#2141-2143)

#### pub fn [get_query_str](https://docs.rs#method.get_query_str)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>

Get the query component of the request URL, if it exists, as a percent-encoded ASCII string.

This is a shorthand for `self.get_url().query()`; see [ Url::query()](https://docs.rs/http/struct.Url.html#method.query) for details and other
query manipulation functions.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#2159-2166)#### pub fn [get_query_parameter](https://docs.rs#method.get_query_parameter)(&self, parameter: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#2159-2166)

#### pub fn [get_query_parameter](https://docs.rs#method.get_query_parameter)(&self, parameter: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>

Get the value of a query parameter in the request’s URL.

This assumes that the query string is a `&` separated list of `parameter=value` pairs.  The
value of the first occurrence of `parameter` is returned. No URL decoding is performed.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-48)Examples

```
let req = Request::get("https://example.com/page?foo=bar&baz=qux");
assert_eq!(req.get_query_parameter("foo"), Some("bar"));
assert_eq!(req.get_query_parameter("baz"), Some("qux"));
assert_eq!(req.get_query_parameter("other"), None);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#2213-2215)#### pub fn [get_query](https://docs.rs#method.get_query)<T: [DeserializeOwned](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/wasm32-wasip1/serde_core/de/trait.DeserializeOwned.html)>(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, [Error](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/wasm32-wasip1/serde_core/de/value/struct.Error.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#2213-2215)

#### pub fn [get_query](https://docs.rs#method.get_query)<T: [DeserializeOwned](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/wasm32-wasip1/serde_core/de/trait.DeserializeOwned.html)>(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, [Error](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/wasm32-wasip1/serde_core/de/value/struct.Error.html)>

Attempt to parse the query component of the request URL into the specified datatype.

The return type chosen for this function must implement [ serde::de::Deserialize](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/wasm32-wasip1/serde_core/de/trait.Deserialize.html) without any
non-static lifetimes; see the trait documentation for details.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-4)Errors

This method returns [ serde_urlencoded::de::Error](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/wasm32-wasip1/serde_core/de/value/struct.Error.html) if deserialization fails.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-49)Examples

Parsing into a vector of string pairs:

```
let req = Request::get("https://example.com/foo?hello=%F0%9F%8C%90!&bar=baz");
let pairs: Vec<(String, String)> = req.get_query().unwrap();
assert_eq!((pairs[0].0.as_str(), pairs[0].1.as_str()), ("hello", "🌐!"));
```
Parsing into a mapping between strings (note that duplicates are removed since
[ HashMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/collections/hash/map/struct.HashMap.html) is not a multimap):

```
use std::collections::HashMap;
let req = Request::get("https://example.com/foo?hello=%F0%9F%8C%90!&bar=baz&bar=quux");
let map: HashMap<String, String> = req.get_query().unwrap();
assert_eq!(map.len(), 2);
assert_eq!(map["hello"].as_str(), "🌐!");
```
Parsing into a custom type that derives [ serde::de::Deserialize](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/wasm32-wasip1/serde_core/de/trait.Deserialize.html):

```
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct MyData {
    name: String,
    count: u64,
}
let mut req = Request::get("https://example.com/?name=Computers&count=1024");
let my_data = req.take_body_form::<MyData>().unwrap();
assert_eq!(&my_data.name, "Computers");
assert_eq!(my_data.count, 1024);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#2234-2236)#### pub fn [set_query_str](https://docs.rs#method.set_query_str)(&mut self, query: impl [AsRef](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.AsRef.html)<[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#2234-2236)

#### pub fn [set_query_str](https://docs.rs#method.set_query_str)(&mut self, query: impl [AsRef](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.AsRef.html)<[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>)

Set the query string of the request URL query component to the given string, performing percent-encoding if necessary.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-50)Examples

```
let mut req = Request::get("https://example.com/foo");
req.set_query_str("hello=🌐!&bar=baz");
assert_eq!(req.get_url_str(), "https://example.com/foo?hello=%F0%9F%8C%90!&bar=baz");
```
Convert the given value to `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` format and set that data as
the request URL query component.

The given value must implement [ serde::Serialize](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/wasm32-wasip1/serde_core/ser/trait.Serialize.html); see the trait documentation for
details.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-5)Errors

This method returns [ serde_urlencoded::ser::Error](https://docs.rs/serde_urlencoded/0.7.1/wasm32-wasip1/serde_urlencoded/ser/enum.Error.html) if serialization fails.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-51)Examples

```
#[derive(serde::Serialize)]
struct MyData {
    name: String,
    count: u64,
}
let my_data = MyData { name: "Computers".to_string(), count: 1024 };
let mut req = Request::get("https://example.com/foo");
req.set_query(&my_data).unwrap();
assert_eq!(req.get_url_str(), "https://example.com/foo?name=Computers&count=1024");
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#2290-2292)#### pub fn [remove_query](https://docs.rs#method.remove_query)(&mut self)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#2290-2292)

#### pub fn [remove_query](https://docs.rs#method.remove_query)(&mut self)

Remove the query component from the request URL, if one exists.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-52)Examples

```
let mut req = Request::get("https://example.com/foo?hello=%F0%9F%8C%90!&bar=baz");
req.remove_query();
assert_eq!(req.get_url_str(), "https://example.com/foo");
```
Set whether this request should be cached if sent to a backend.

By default this is `false`, which means the backend will only be reached if a cached
response is not available. Set this to `true` to send the request directly to the backend
without caching.

[§](https://docs.rs#overrides)Overrides

Note that calling [ set_pass(true)](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_pass) will override anything previously set by

[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_surrogate_key)

`Request::set_surrogate_key`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_ttl)

`Request::set_stale_while_revalidate``set_pass`,
then you may want to instead use the [equivalents of those methods inside of a](https://docs.rs/http/struct.CandidateResponse.html)

`CandidateResponse`[callback.](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_after_send)

`Request::set_after_send`Conversely, calling any of those methods on Request *after* calling `set_pass(true)` will
reverse the effect of the `set_pass` call, and any response received when the
request is sent may become cacheable.

Override the caching behavior of this request to enable or disable PCI/HIPAA-compliant non-volatile caching.

By default, this is `false`, which means the request may not be PCI/HIPAA-compliant. Set it
to `true` to enable compliant caching.

documentation](https://docs.fastly.com/products/pci-compliant-caching-and-delivery) for
details.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#2435-2437)#### pub fn [set_surrogate_key](https://docs.rs#method.set_surrogate_key)(&mut self, sk: [HeaderValue](https://docs.rs/http/struct.HeaderValue.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#2435-2437)

#### pub fn [set_surrogate_key](https://docs.rs#method.set_surrogate_key)(&mut self, sk: [HeaderValue](https://docs.rs/http/struct.HeaderValue.html))

Override the caching behavior of this request to include the given surrogate key(s), provided as a header value.

The header value can contain more than one surrogate key, separated by spaces.

Surrogate keys must contain only printable ASCII characters (those between `0x21` and
`0x7E`, inclusive). Any invalid keys will be ignored.

See the [Fastly surrogate keys
guide](https://docs.fastly.com/en/guides/purging-api-cache-with-surrogate-keys) for details.

[§](https://docs.rs#overrides-5)Overrides

This overrides any previous [ Request::set_pass](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_pass) call and sets the

`pass` behavior to
`false`, and extends (but does not replace) any `Surrogate-Key` response headers from the
backend.Note that calling [ set_pass(true)](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_pass) will override anything previously set by

[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_surrogate_key)

`Request::set_surrogate_key`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_ttl)

`Request::set_ttl`[, and](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_pci)

`Request::set_pci`[. If you wish to unconditionally call](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_stale_while_revalidate)

`Request::set_stale_while_revalidate``set_pass`,
then you may want to instead use the [equivalents of those methods inside of a](https://docs.rs/http/struct.CandidateResponse.html)

`CandidateResponse`[callback.](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_after_send)

`Request::set_after_send`Conversely, calling any of those methods on Request *after* calling `set_pass(true)` will

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#2599-2602)#### pub fn [get_tls_client_cert_verify_result](https://docs.rs#method.get_tls_client_cert_verify_result)(
    &self,
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[ClientCertVerifyResult](https://docs.rs/fastly-shared/0.13.0/wasm32-wasip1/fastly_shared/enum.ClientCertVerifyResult.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#2599-2602)

#### pub fn [get_tls_client_cert_verify_result](https://docs.rs#method.get_tls_client_cert_verify_result)(
    &self,
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[ClientCertVerifyResult](https://docs.rs/fastly-shared/0.13.0/wasm32-wasip1/fastly_shared/enum.ClientCertVerifyResult.html)>

Returns the error code defined in ClientCertVerifyResult.

If your service is set up for mTLS (see [this documentation](https://docs.fastly.com/en/guides/setting-up-mutual-tls-authentication)),
then this will return information about the client’s mTLS certificate, if provided.
If the certificate is not provided, you will receive a `ClientCertVerifyResult::CertificateMissing`
value, if the certificate properly matches your mTLS configuration, you will receive
a `ClientCertVerifyResult::Ok`, etc.

If your service is *not* set up for mTLS, this function will always return
`Some(ClientCertVerifyResult::Ok)`.

If you have a service that may be run with some domains that are mTLS protected,
and some that are not mTLS protected, then we advise checking for both the existence
of a certificate (by verifying that `get_tls_raw_client_certificate` or
`get_tls_raw_client_certificate_bytes` return `Some`) before checking the result of
this function. Doing both makes sure that you both received a certificate and that
it was valid, and will work for both the mTLS-protected and non-mTLS-protected
domains.

This function returns `None` in the case that this `Request` is not from the
client, but was instead generated by other parts of the code. (In other words,
it will return `None` if this request was neither the argument to a function marked
`fastly::main` nor generated with `Request::from_client`.)

Get the cipher suite used to secure the client TLS connection, as a string, panicking if it is not UTF-8.

The value returned will be consistent with the [OpenSSL
name](https://testssl.sh/openssl-iana.mapping.html) for the cipher suite.

Returns `None` if this is not the client request.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-53)Examples

```
assert_eq!(
    Request::from_client().get_tls_cipher_openssl_name().unwrap(),
    Some("ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256"),
);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#2682-2686)

#### pub fn [set_auto_decompress_gzip](https://docs.rs#method.set_auto_decompress_gzip)(&mut self, gzip: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Set whether a `gzip`-encoded response to this request will be automatically decompressed.

Enabling this will set the `Accept-Encoding` header before the request is sent, regardless
of the original value in the request, to ensure that any values originally sent by a
browser or other client get replaced with `gzip`, so that the backend will not try sending
unsupported compression algorithms.

If the response to this request is `gzip`-encoded, it will be presented in decompressed
form, and the `Content-Encoding` and `Content-Length` headers will be removed.

Send this request on behalf of another service.

Running it on behalf of another service means that the cache store used for this request will be of that service, not the currently running one.

[§](https://docs.rs#internal--privileged)Internal / Privileged

This operation is privileged, and attempts to use this functionality without proper privileges will cause errors. If you are interested in having two or more of your services share the same cache, please talk to your Fastly account representative. While we have no plans to offer this ability widely – this capability is only currently allowed for Fastly-internal services – we may revisit this decision given sufficient customer input.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#3039-3041)#### pub fn [set_image_optimizer](https://docs.rs#method.set_image_optimizer)(&mut self, options: [ImageOptimizerOptions](https://docs.rs/image_optimizer/struct.ImageOptimizerOptions.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/request.rs.html#3039-3041)

#### pub fn [set_image_optimizer](https://docs.rs#method.set_image_optimizer)(&mut self, options: [ImageOptimizerOptions](https://docs.rs/image_optimizer/struct.ImageOptimizerOptions.html))

Set [ image_optimizer::ImageOptimizerOptions](https://docs.rs/image_optimizer/struct.ImageOptimizerOptions.html) for this request to proxy it
to Image Optimizer.

Transformations can be expressed through `ImageOptimizerOptions`
or query parameters on the request. Options set on `ImageOptimizerOptions`
take precedence over query parameters with the same name.

It is not necessary to include additional shielding logic for Image Optimization,
the required [ ImageOptimizerRegion](https://docs.rs/image_optimizer/enum.ImageOptimizerRegion.html)
handles this for you. It is recommended to pick a region close to your origin.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-57)Examples

Send a request for `image.jpeg` with params `format=webp` to Image Optimizer.

```
let mut image_opto_opts = ImageOptimizerOptions::from_region(ImageOptimizerRegion::UsWest);
image_opto_opts.format = Some(Format::WebP);
let mut req = Request::get("https://example.com/image.jpeg");
req.set_image_optimizer(image_opto_opts);
// `origin` is a named backend on your service.
req.send("origin")?;
```
Override the `format` parameter on the request if it exists, turning it to `auto`.

```
#[fastly::main]
fn main(mut req: Request) -> Result<Response, Error> {
let mut image_opto_opts = ImageOptimizerOptions::from_region(ImageOptimizerRegion::UsWest);
if let Some(_param) = req.get_query_parameter("format") {
    image_opto_opts.format = Some(Format::Auto);
}
req.set_image_optimizer(image_opto_opts);
Ok(req.send("origin")?)
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#overrides-6)Overrides

At the moment, calling this function overrides custom caching behavior, such as
[ Request::set_surrogate_key()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_surrogate_key),

[and](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_ttl)

`Request::set_ttl()`[. Caching behavior is currently determined by the cache control headers set on the source image.](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.set_pci)

`Request::set_pci()`Additionally, any before and after send hooks are not executed.

`Box<dyn Trait>` (where `Trait: Downcast`) to `Box<dyn Any>`. `Box<dyn Any>` can
then be further `downcast` into `Box<ConcreteType>` where `ConcreteType` implements `Trait`.`Rc<Trait>` (where `Trait: Downcast`) to `Rc<Any>`. `Rc<Any>` can then be

# Response in fastly - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fastly/0.13.0/fastly/struct.Response.html

`pub struct Response { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An HTTP response, including body, headers, and status code.

[§](https://docs.rs#sending-to-the-client)Sending to the client

Each execution of a Compute program may send a single response back to the client:

If no response is explicitly sent by the program, a default `200 OK` response is sent.

[§](https://docs.rs#creation-and-conversion)Creation and conversion

Responses can be created programmatically:

Responses are also returned from backend requests:

For interoperability with other Rust libraries, [ Response](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html) can be converted to and from the

[crate’s](https://docs.rs/http/1.3.1/wasm32-wasip1/http/index.html)

`http`[type using the](https://docs.rs/http/1.3.1/wasm32-wasip1/http/response/struct.Response.html)

`http::Response`[and](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.from)

`From`[traits.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html#tymethod.into)

`Into`[§](https://docs.rs#builder-style-methods)Builder-style methods

[ Response](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html) can be used as a

[builder](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.0.0/style/ownership/builders.html), allowing responses to be constructed and used through method chaining. Methods with the

`with_` name prefix, such as
[, return](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.with_header)

`with_header()``Self` to allow chaining. The builder style is
typically most useful when constructing and using a response in a single expression. For
example:```
Response::new()
    .with_header("my-header", "hello!")
    .with_header("my-other-header", "Здравствуйте!")
    .send_to_client();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#setter-methods)Setter methods

Setter methods, such as [ set_header()](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.set_header), are prefixed by

`set_`, and can
be used interchangeably with the builder-style methods, allowing you to mix and match styles
based on what is most convenient for your program. Setter methods tend to work better than
builder-style methods when constructing a value involves conditional branches or loops. For
example:```
let mut resp = Response::new().with_header("my-header", "hello!");
if needs_translation {
    resp.set_header("my-other-header", "Здравствуйте!");
}
resp.send_to_client();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/response.rs.html#190-199)#### pub fn [clone_without_body](https://docs.rs#method.clone_without_body)(&self) -> [Response](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/response.rs.html#190-199)

#### pub fn [clone_without_body](https://docs.rs#method.clone_without_body)(&self) -> [Response](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html)

Make a new response with the same headers, status, and version of this response, but no body.

If you also need to clone the response body, use
`clone_with_body()`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
let original = Response::from_body("hello")
    .with_header("hello", "world!")
    .with_status(418);
let new = original.clone_without_body();
assert_eq!(original.get_header("hello"), new.get_header("hello"));
assert_eq!(original.get_status(), new.get_status());
assert_eq!(original.get_version(), new.get_version());
assert!(original.has_body());
assert!(!new.has_body());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/response.rs.html#222-246)#### pub fn [clone_with_body](https://docs.rs#method.clone_with_body)(&mut self) -> [Response](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/response.rs.html#222-246)

#### pub fn [clone_with_body](https://docs.rs#method.clone_with_body)(&mut self) -> [Response](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html)

Clone this response by reading in its body, and then writing the same body to the original and the cloned response.

This method requires mutable access to this response because reading from and writing to the body can involve an HTTP connection.

This operation is potentially expensive if the body is large. Take care when using this
method on bodies with unknown sizes. Consider using methods like [ BufRead::lines()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.BufRead.html#method.lines) or

[to incrementally process a body while limiting the maximum size.](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html#method.read_chunks)

`Body::read_chunks()`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
let mut original = Response::from_body("hello")
    .with_header("hello", "world!")
    .with_status(418);
let mut new = original.clone_with_body();
assert_eq!(original.get_header("hello"), new.get_header("hello"));
assert_eq!(original.get_status(), new.get_status());
assert_eq!(original.get_version(), new.get_version());
assert_eq!(original.take_body_bytes(), new.take_body_bytes());
```
Create a new [ Response](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html) with the given value as the body.

[§](https://docs.rs#argument-type-conversion)Argument type conversion

See the `From` impls for [ Body](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html) to see which types can be used as a body.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
let resp = Response::from_body("hello");
assert_eq!(&resp.into_body_str(), "hello");
```
```
let body_bytes: &[u8] = &[1, 2, 3];
let resp = Response::from_body(body_bytes);
assert_eq!(resp.into_body_bytes().as_slice(), body_bytes);
```

#### pub fn [get_body_mut](https://docs.rs#method.get_body_mut)(&mut self) -> &mut [Body](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html) [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Get a mutable reference to the body of this response.

An empty body is returned if no body has been set, or if it has previously been returned by a method
like [ take_body()](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.take_body).

```

assert_eq!(&resp.into_body_str(), "hello, world!");
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/response.rs.html#416-418)#### pub fn [get_body_prefix_str_mut](https://docs.rs#method.get_body_prefix_str_mut)(&mut self, length: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [PrefixString](https://docs.rs/http/body/struct.PrefixString.html)<'_>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/response.rs.html#416-418)

#### pub fn [get_body_prefix_str_mut](https://docs.rs#method.get_body_prefix_str_mut)(&mut self, length: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [PrefixString](https://docs.rs/http/body/struct.PrefixString.html)<'_>

Get a prefix of this response’s body as a string containing up to the given number of bytes.

See [ Body::get_prefix_str_mut()](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html#method.get_prefix_str_mut) for details.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

If the prefix contains invalid UTF-8 bytes, this function will panic. The exception to this is if the bytes are invalid because a multi-byte codepoint is cut off by the requested prefix length. In this case, the invalid bytes are left off the end of the prefix.

To explicitly handle the possibility of invalid UTF-8 bytes, use
[ try_get_body_prefix_str_mut()](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.try_get_body_prefix_str_mut), which returns an
error on failure rather than panicking.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/response.rs.html#476-482)#### pub fn [append_body](https://docs.rs#method.append_body)(&mut self, other: [Body](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/response.rs.html#476-482)

#### pub fn [append_body](https://docs.rs#method.append_body)(&mut self, other: [Body](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html))

Append another [ Body](https://docs.rs/struct.Body.html) to the body of this response without reading or writing any body
contents.

If this response does not have a body, the appended body is set as the response’s body.

This operation is performed in amortized constant time, and so should always be preferred to reading an entire body and then writing the same contents to another body.

This method should be used when combining bodies that have not necessarily been read yet,
such as a body returned from a backend response. To append contents that are already in
memory as strings or bytes, use [ get_body_mut()](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.get_body_mut) to write the
contents to the end of the body.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-9)Examples

```
let mut resp = Response::from_body("hello! backend says: ");
let backend_resp = Request::get("https://example.com/").send("example_backend")?;
resp.append_body(backend_resp.into_body());
resp.send_to_client();
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/response.rs.html#494-496)#### pub fn [into_body_bytes](https://docs.rs#method.into_body_bytes)(self) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/response.rs.html#494-496)

#### pub fn [into_body_bytes](https://docs.rs#method.into_body_bytes)(self) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Consume the response and return its body as a byte vector.

[§](https://docs.rs#memory-usage)Memory usage

This method will cause the entire body to be buffering in WebAssembly memory. You should take care
not to exceed the WebAssembly memory limits, and consider using methods like
[ read_body_lines()](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.read_body_lines) or

[to control how much of the body you process at once.](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.read_body_chunks)

`read_body_chunks()`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-10)Examples

```
let resp = Response::from_body("hello, world!");
let bytes = resp.into_body_bytes();
assert_eq!(&bytes, b"hello, world!");
```

#### pub fn [into_body_str_lossy](https://docs.rs#method.into_body_str_lossy)(self) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

Consume the response and return its body as a string, including invalid characters.

Only the valid UTF-8 characters present are returned.
Invalid UTF-8 characters are replaced with [ U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/char/constant.REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#memory-usage-2)Memory usage

This method will cause the entire body to be buffering in WebAssembly memory. You should take care
not to exceed the WebAssembly memory limits, and consider using methods like
[ read_body_lines()](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.read_body_lines) or

[to control how much of the body you process at once.](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.read_body_chunks)

`read_body_chunks()`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-12)Examples

```
let mut resp = Response::new();
resp.set_body_octet_stream(b"\xF0\x90\x80 hello, world!");
let string = resp.into_body_str_lossy();
assert_eq!(&string, "� hello, world!");
```

assert_eq!(&resp.into_body_str(), "<p>hello, world!</p>");
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/response.rs.html#618-624)#### pub fn [take_body_str](https://docs.rs#method.take_body_str)(&mut self) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fastly/http/response.rs.html#618-624)

#### pub fn [take_body_str](https://docs.rs#method.take_body_str)(&mut self) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

Take and return the body from this response as a string.

After calling this method, this response will no longer have a body.

[§](https://docs.rs#memory-usage-3)Memory usage

This method will cause the entire body to be buffering in WebAssembly memory. You should take care
not to exceed the WebAssembly memory limits, and consider using methods like
[ read_body_lines()](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.read_body_lines) or

[to control how much of the body you process at once.](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.read_body_chunks)

`read_body_chunks()`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-2)Panics

If the body does not contain a valid UTF-8 string, this function will panic. To handle the
possibility of invalid UTF-8 data, use [ take_body_str_lossy()](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.take_body_str_lossy) for
lossy conversion, or use

[and then convert the bytes with a function like](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.take_body_bytes)

`take_body_bytes()`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.from_utf8)

`String::from_utf8`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-15)Examples

```
let mut resp = Response::from_body("hello, world!");
let string = resp.take_body_str();
assert!(resp.try_take_body().is_none());
assert_eq!(&string, "hello, world!");
```

After calling this method, this response will no longer have a body.
